knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ k\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the augmented matrix for $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ to determine when the system is consistent:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} &=-1 \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=0 \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=k\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & k + 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(1)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k \\ k &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=1$ and $x_1=-2$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(-2)\mathbf{a}_1+(1)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=0$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ k \\ -7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the augmented matrix for $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ to determine when the system is consistent:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & k \\ 1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} &=-3 \\ 2 x_{1} - 2 x_{2} &=k \\ x_{1} - 2 x_{2} &=-7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & k \\ 1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

Place the two known-coordinate equations first (a row permutation).

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 2 & -2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & k + 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow (-1)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & k + 6\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k + 6$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k + 6 \\ k &=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=4$ and $x_1=1$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(1)\mathbf{a}_1+(4)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -6 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=-6$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 9 \\ k\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the augmented matrix for $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ to determine when the system is consistent:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 9 \\ -1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} &=5 \\ x_{1} - 2 x_{2} &=9 \\ - x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=k\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 9 \\ -1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & k + 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow (-1)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & k + 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(1)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & k + 9\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k + 9$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k + 9 \\ k &=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=-4$ and $x_1=1$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(1)\mathbf{a}_1+(-4)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 9 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=-9$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.
